model_system: single-domain nanoscale chiral antiferromagnet Mn3Sn (Mn3X family), modeled as three coupled classical magnetization vectors representing the six-spin kagome unit cell

key_params.free_energy: F = sum_{i!=j}[J_{ij} m_i·m_j + D_{ij} zhat·(m_i×m_j)] - sum_i K_i (m_i·e_i)^2
key_params.symmetry_breaking: J12 = J(1-nu), all other couplings intrinsic
key_params.temperature_regimes: low-barrier Delta << kT; high-barrier Delta > kT

headline_claim: Octupole relaxation in chiral AFM nanomagnets can reach picosecond timescales in the low-barrier regime, with electrical tuning by orders of magnitude via spin-orbit torque.
replication_difficulty: medium-high: stochastic LLG is straightforward in principle, but reproducing the claimed picosecond relaxation and crossover needs full paper/SI parameters, thermal-noise implementation, and volume/barrier calibration.
